chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
Regarding a woman who slandered her husband, and he was deaf, he (peace be upon him) said: 'They are separated between her and him, and she is not permissible for him ever.'

key_terms.قَذَفَتْ: Slandered (specifically in the context of hadd al-ridud or general accusation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a deaf husband if his wife slanders him?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights a distinct jurisprudential position where the wife's slander (qadhf) against her deaf husband results in permanent separation (la tahillu lahu abadan), differing from the standard three-divorce rule. Scholars note that the husband's deafness may preclude him from effectively exercising the right to revoke the divorce or from being a valid witness in the same manner, thereby solidifying the finality of the bond's dissolution. This emphasizes the gravity of false accusation within the marital contract in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: From him, from Al Hassan, from one of his companions,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a woman whose husband slandered her, and he was deaf. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There would be separation between her and him, and she would not be Permissible for him, ever’.
en.sarwar: It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from al-Hassan from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “About the case of a woman who accuses her husband who is speechless, abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al- Salam, has said, ‘They are separated from each other and he is not lawful for her forever.’”
